explanation: The assassination article puts the dismissal and the coup that followed it at the head of the sequence that ends in the killing: "Following the September 1960 coup led by Mobutu Sese Seko, Lumumba and his political retinue were detained by Mobutu's forces in December 1960. After a month of imprisonment near Léopoldville, he was transferred to Belgium-aligned Katanga in mid-January." The coup article carries the same chain with the custody in it. Mobutu "privately aligned himself with Kasa-Vubu at the expense of Lumumba, placing him under house arrest", and "In December 1960, Lumumba was captured while attempting to escape house arrest and subsequently transferred to Katanga, then a secessionist province led by Moïse Tshombe, where he was held." The type is `enabled` because the dismissal produced the custody that made the killing possible. Both articles agree that the order to kill came from the Katangan authorities rather than from Léopoldville. The confidence is `probable` because Wikipedia is the only source (rule 22).
